description: Twenty synthetic reporting defects for gold-label recall testing.

cases.text: Six mice contributed ten cells each; n=60 independent replicates.
Each participant was measured five times and all observations were analyzed as independent.
Sample size was selected from laboratory habit; no precision or power rationale was used.
The difference was significant at P=0.04; no magnitude or interval was reported.
Twenty primary outcomes were each tested at alpha 0.05 without correction.
Error bars are shown but neither their definition nor what each point represents is stated.
The abstract reports a 20% increase while Table 2 reports an 18% decrease.
Fifteen percent of participants were lost; missingness and analysis population were not described.
P=0.12 was interpreted as proof that treatments are equivalent.
A subgroup selected after viewing results was presented as confirmatory.
Three technical PCR wells were described as three biological replicates.
Cluster-randomized schools were analyzed at student level without cluster adjustment.
A paired crossover design was analyzed with an unpaired test.
Outliers were removed after analysis, but no rule or excluded count was reported.
Methods state a two-sided test; Results report a one-sided P value.
A confidence interval excludes zero but the reported two-sided P value is 0.21.
The model assumes proportional hazards; no assessment is reported despite crossing curves.
The outcome unit is mg/L in Methods and mmol/L in Figure 3 without conversion.
Enrollment was 120, exclusions were 10, but the analysis denominator is reported as 125.
The primary endpoint in the registry differs from the endpoint labeled primary in the manuscript.
